definition.en: Discrimination that arises when a seemingly neutral provision, criterion, or practice disproportionately disadvantages persons with a protected characteristic, unless the measure is objectively justified by a legitimate aim and the means of achieving it are appropriate and necessary. For example: a workplace rule requiring full-time on-site presence may disproportionately exclude employees with disabilities or caregiving responsibilities if reasonable adjustments could achieve the same goal without exclusion.

en: This concept, developed in U.S. equal protection and EU equality law, recognises that discrimination often operates structurally, through rules and decisions that perpetuate inequality even without explicit bias
